articles.title: Theme & Appearance
articles.summary: Four theme variants, eight customizable accent colors, and independent zoom for every UI surface.

beginner.text: Settings → Theme offers Dark (default), Slate, Light, and Cream. Switching applies live to every surface — modals, popup, editor, shelf — no reload needed.
Color pickers let you override the brand accent, action-button colors, and the four status colors (error, warning, success, info). All tinted backgrounds and borders derive from these automatically.

Each surface has its own zoom slider (50–150%): modals, popovers, toasts, the shelf, the popup, the editor, and the playground. Scale just the things you find small without blowing up the whole browser.

articles.title: Feature Toggles
articles.summary: Every feature can be switched on or off independently. This reference is generated from the live registry, so it always matches your build.

beginner.text: Settings → Features lists a switch per feature, grouped by area. Turning one off removes its buttons, shortcuts, and shelf actions everywhere — instantly. Everything defaults to ON except Power Automate.
Missing a toggle from this list in your Settings? An admin may have hidden it — see "Hidden Settings" in the Power User Corner.

articles.title: Keyboard Shortcuts (Settings)
articles.summary: Rebind the four global shortcut letters — Task List, Margin Calculator, CRM Search, and New Contact.

beginner.text: Change the letter under Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts. The modifier is always Ctrl (Cmd on Mac). A shortcut only works while its feature toggle is on.

articles.title: Custom CRM Pages
articles.summary: Replace selected CRM pages (dashboard, search, task list, …) with the extension's own UI.

advanced.text: Settings → Custom Pages exposes one switch per registered page scope. Enabling CRM activates the extension interface on supported CRM takeovers; disabling it uses the stock CRM pages. Scope values and visibility can be centrally managed by the authenticated policy.
Page overrides change what teammates see if you share a preset that includes them. Keep overrides out of shared presets unless the whole team wants them.

articles.title: Email & Integrations
articles.summary: Your signature, the Power Automate flow that powers silent sending, and the Microsoft sign-in behind draft replies.

rows: HTML signature appended automatically to every Power Automate send (not to Outlook-fallback emails).
Master switch for silent sending. ON + a valid flow URL = emails send in the background. OFF = pre-filled Outlook windows.
The local-part of your From address (Developer Settings). Set it to your own account on day one.
Authorizes draft creation in your mailbox for reply-with-template. Drafts only — never auto-sends.

advanced.text: The Power Automate flow receives a JSON payload with the email list and an attachments array of inline images; the flow forwards both to its Outlook send action. If images arrive broken in recipients' clients, the flow is likely dropping the attachments array.

articles.title: Developer Settings
articles.summary: Every fine-tuning knob in one generated table: animation timing, draggable modals, catalog cache, 3D viewer tuning, and snapshot poses.

advanced.text: Developer Settings holds the low-stakes knobs that don't deserve a top-level toggle. They're grouped below exactly as registered in the build you're running — defaults, ranges, and descriptions come straight from the code.
The authenticated remote policy can manage these values or hide this section. RevStack dashboard administrators bypass that policy.

articles.title: Shared Settings Templates
articles.summary: Bundle selected settings and templates under a name, receive a revocable URL, and let another enrolled installation preview and choose what to import.

intermediate.text: Settings → Shared Settings Templates stores selected scopes on RevStack under a name and returns an opaque URL. A recipient pastes that URL into their extension, previews the name and included scopes, and chooses what to import:
No file is downloaded or uploaded. Both creator and recipient authenticate through their own extension installation. The creator can list and revoke links created by that installation.

advanced.text: Settings scopes overwrite on import. Template scopes merge by id: a template with the same id replaces yours, a new id appends. Importing never deletes templates that only exist on your side.

Treat the opaque URL as a capability and share it only with intended recipients. Credentials, installation auth, Watch List data, and administrator policy are never included; managed policy is reapplied independently after import.
